choices.label: Ask CaldovaIQ what the contracts say
choices.user: Contoso and Litware over-delivered by more than 10%, Fabrikam under-delivered. What do their contracts say for each of them?
choices.assistant: Three advertisers, three different treatments. Contoso Mobility's contract (ZM-ADV-001-2026) grants a credit, Litware Retail's explicitly excludes any compensation for over-delivery, and Fabrikam Beauty's triggers a penalty for under-delivery.
choices.reflection:
**Contoso Mobility — ZM-ADV-001-2026 → credit**
- Art. 5.2: approved plans are the contracted volume.
- Art. 6.1: excess above 5% is not billable.
- Art. 6.2: above 10%, a credit of 50% of the media value of the excess at the channel net rate, applied to the next quarter and issued within 45 days — **without any request from the advertiser**.
- Art. 6.4: assessed per market, no compensation between markets.

**Litware Retail — ZM-ADV-004-2026 → excluded**
- Art. 6.1: no compensation for over-delivery.
- Art. 6.2: the advertiser cannot claim any benefit from over-delivery.
- Art. 6.3: nothing is billed above the budget.
- Art. 9.2: claims are closed after 120 days.

**Fabrikam Beauty — Art. 6.2 → penalty**
- Under-delivery beyond tolerance costs 2% of the net media budget.

choices.label: Build the delivery compensation plan — Fabric IQ + Foundry IQ
choices.assistant: Here are three ways to settle Q3. All of them respect the contracts; they differ on how proactive we are with Contoso.
choices.chain: Caldova Media Agent → Delivery Analyst → Contracts Agent

scenarios.title: Scenario 1 — Contract minimum
scenarios.body: Issue the Contoso credit within the 45-day window, apply the Fabrikam penalty, no action on Litware. Lowest effort, but Contoso hears about the credit only from the invoice.
scenarios.supportedBy: Supported by Foundry IQ (Contoso contract) · Foundry IQ (Fabrikam contract)
scenarios.response: That works contractually, but it carries a relationship risk: Contoso would learn about the credit only from the invoice, after Finance already flagged it on 2026-10-12. It also misses the EV roadshow in Spain (2–15 Nov), where the credit could become visible bonus inventory. I'd recommend Scenario 2.

scenarios.title: Scenario 2 — Recommended
scenarios.body: Apply the Contoso credit as Q4 bonus inventory on the EV roadshow (2–15 Nov), announced proactively by Marta Gil. Apply the Fabrikam penalty per Art. 6.2. For Litware, no compensation (Art. 6.1) but a transparent explanation at the QBR.
scenarios.supportedBy: Supported by Fabric IQ (delivery vs. contract) · Foundry IQ (Contoso contract) · Foundry IQ (Litware contract) · Work IQ (Finance note) · Web IQ (Contoso EV launch)

scenarios.title: Scenario 3 — Goodwill for everyone
scenarios.body: Credit both Contoso and Litware. Commercially generous, but Litware's contract excludes it — it creates a precedent outside policy.
scenarios.response: Generous, but risky: Art. 6.1 of the Litware contract excludes any compensation for over-delivery. Crediting Litware would set a precedent outside policy that other advertisers could invoke. I'd recommend Scenario 2 — same goodwill for Contoso, transparency for Litware.

choices.label: Prepare the Litware QBR message
choices.user: Help me prepare how we explain the Q3 over-delivery at the Litware Retail QBR.
choices.assistant: Litware received 11.0% more impressions than planned, but its contract excludes any compensation. Here are three ways to present it.
choices.chain: Caldova Media Agent → Delivery Analyst → Contracts Agent

scenarios.title: Option 1 — Footnote
scenarios.body: Mention the over-delivery as a line in the delivery slide. Minimal, but Litware may discover the comparison with other advertisers later.
scenarios.supportedBy: Supported by Fabric IQ (delivery vs. contract)
scenarios.response: A footnote is low effort, but Litware may later spot the +11.0% when comparing with other advertisers — and a buried number reads as something hidden. Option 2 frames it openly as added reach at no cost (Art. 6.1 and 6.3), tied to the Litware Home promotion (26 Oct – 8 Nov).

scenarios.title: Option 2 — Recommended
scenarios.body: Present the +11.0% transparently as added reach at no cost, cite Art. 6.1 and 6.3 (no compensation, nothing billed above budget), and tie it to the Litware Home promotion (26 Oct – 8 Nov).
scenarios.supportedBy: Supported by Fabric IQ (delivery vs. contract) · Foundry IQ (Litware contract) · Web IQ (Litware Home promo)

scenarios.title: Option 3 — Separate note
scenarios.body: Send a dedicated note before the QBR. Clear, but it gives the topic more weight than the contract does.
scenarios.response: A dedicated note is clear, but it signals an issue where the contract sees none: Art. 6.1 excludes compensation, so a standalone note invites a negotiation. I'd recommend Option 2 — cover it inside the QBR, linked to the Litware Home promotion (26 Oct – 8 Nov).
